_doc: MEMORY.md index lines on which every parser of index lines must name the same entry file (backlog item 169). The index format is `- [Title](file.md) [tags] — hook`, so the entry's own file is the target of the FIRST `](….md)` on the line; a link or a `(name.md)` in the hook text is not the entry. Before the fix, the awk matcher in hooks/lib/memory-tags.sh (behind the §11 deny and the memory hint), parseMemoryIndex in scripts/lib/memory-tags.js (the doctor's tag scan) and scripts/spec-coherence-audit.js took the LAST `(….md)` on the line: on lines[0] the coherence audit reported feedback_old.md dangling and feedback_a.md not indexed, and on lines[1] and lines[3] the other two named feedback_old.md. hooks/mem-audit.sh read the first `](`, but its sed could not reach one that follows a `]`, so it found no link on lines[4]. Fields per line — line: written verbatim into a sandbox MEMORY.md; file: the entry file every parser must report; tags: what the two tag parsers must report for it ([] = untagged, which both skip). onDisk: the memory files the drift parsers run against. neverAnEntry: must not appear in any parser's output. Read by tests/scripts/memory-index-links.test.js, tests/hooks/memory-tags-parity.test.sh, tests/hooks/mem-audit.test.sh, tests/hooks/memory-read-check.test.sh and tests/hooks/memory-prompt-hint.test.sh.

the same shape with a tag block, so the tag parsers report it at all
control: an ordinary line whose only link is the entry's own
